record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Develop phase-space analysis and non-perturbative methods for quantum field theory directly in Minkowski space, with the goal of obtaining the first proofs of asymptotic completeness for quantum field theory models.

evidence.quote: Develop phase space analysis and non-perturbative methods for field theory that work directly in Minkowski space. This should lead to first proofs of asymptotic completeness

artifact.self_contained_problem: Develop a framework of phase-space analysis and non-perturbative techniques for relativistic quantum field theory formulated directly on Minkowski spacetime (rather than via Euclidean methods followed by Osterwalder–Schrader reconstruction). Concretely, for a nontrivial interacting quantum field theory model satisfying the Wightman or Haag–Kastler axioms in 1+1, 2+1, or 3+1 dimensions, establish asymptotic completeness: prove that the Hilbert space of the theory decomposes as the direct sum of the vacuum subspace and the closed subspaces generated by Haag–Ruelle (or LSZ) scattering states of the stable particle types, i.e. that the incoming and outgoing wave operators are unitary with ranges equal to the full physical Hilbert space. The goal is to obtain the first such proof of asymptotic completeness for any genuinely interacting relativistic quantum field theory model.
artifact.status_search_result: Asymptotic completeness for interacting relativistic quantum field theory models remains a long-standing open problem in constructive QFT. Partial results exist for special low-dimensional models (e.g. weakly coupled P(φ)_2 below the two-particle threshold via Spencer–Zirilli and related work), but a general proof of asymptotic completeness for any interacting QFT, particularly via Minkowski-space phase-space methods, has not been achieved.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotic completeness for P(phi)_2 (Spencer–Zirilli)
status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotic completeness below the three-particle threshold for weakly coupled P(φ)_2 models.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial, low-dimensional, weak-coupling, threshold-restricted asymptotic completeness results are known.

status_evidence.title: Constructive Quantum Field Theory open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotic completeness for interacting QFT remains an outstanding open problem in constructive field theory.
status_evidence.claim: The general problem of proving asymptotic completeness for interacting QFT is open.
